issues.title: No tests for conversion or rounding
issues.comment: Currency conversion is easy to get subtly wrong. Tests for same-currency passthrough, rounding and an unsupported code would lock the behaviour down.

issues.title: Unsupported currencies raise a bare KeyError

issues.title: Rounds every currency to two decimal places
issues.comment: Not every currency has cents: JPY has no minor unit and BHD has three. Quantizing to `0.01` produces amounts the target currency can't represent.

issues.title: Fetches the exchange rate once per amount
issues.comment: `convert_many` calls `get_rate` — a new HTTP client and request — for every amount, so a 1,000-line payout makes 1,000 identical rate requests. Fetch the rate once and convert in memory.
issues.suggested_fix:
if base == quote:

    rate = await get_rate(base, quote)
    return [(amount * rate).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP) for amount in amounts]

issues.title: `Decimal(float)` keeps binary float error
issues.comment: If `payout.amount` is a float, `Decimal(payout.amount)` preserves its binary representation — `Decimal(0.1)` is `0.1000000000000000055511151231257827…` — and the error can survive rounding. Build it from a string.

files.summary: Hash ring with virtual nodes. Lookups past the last hash panic, and hash collisions silently reassign replicas.

issues.title: Hash collisions silently reassign replicas
issues.comment: Two virtual nodes that hash to the same value overwrite each other in `owners`, leaving a duplicate in `hashes` that points at the wrong node. With CRC32 and hundreds of replicas this happens in practice.

issues.title: No tests for distribution or wrap-around
issues.comment: The ring's two core properties — keys spread evenly, and keys above the highest hash wrap to the first node — aren't tested. The wrap-around case would have caught the panic above.

issues.title: Index out of range for keys past the last hash
issues.comment: `sort.Search` returns `len(r.hashes)` when a key hashes above every point on the ring, and indexing with it panics. A ring wraps around — those keys belong to the first point.

issues.title: Removing a node scans the whole ring per replica
issues.comment: `Remove` is O(replicas × ring size). The slice is sorted, so `sort.Search` finds each hash directly.

issues.title: Retries have no jitter
issues.comment: Every failing delivery retries on the same 2, 4, 8… second schedule, so when an endpoint recovers from an outage it receives the backlog in synchronised waves. Add random jitter to the delay.

issues.title: Network errors abort the retry loop

issues.comment: `time.sleep` blocks the event loop, so while one endpoint backs off — up to 64 seconds on the last attempt — every other delivery on this worker stalls too. Use `await asyncio.sleep(...)`.

issues.title: Eviction has no tests
issues.comment: Nothing verifies that expired entries are removed, live ones survive, or that closing `stop` ends the goroutine. A test with a short interval and `-race` would also have caught the locking bug.

issues.title: Ticker is never stopped
issues.comment: When `stop` closes the goroutine returns, but the ticker keeps firing into a channel nobody reads, leaking its timer for the life of the process.

issues.title: Map mutated without holding the cache lock
issues.comment: `evictExpired` runs on its own goroutine and ranges over and deletes from `c.items` without taking `c.mu`, while `Get` and `Set` use the same map under the lock. That's a data race that crashes with `concurrent map iteration and map write`.

issues.title: Clock read once per entry
issues.comment: Calling `time.Now()` inside the loop costs a call per entry and judges entries against a moving clock mid-sweep. Capture `now := time.Now()` once before the loop.

issues.title: A zero TTL expires immediately
issues.comment: `ttl` of `0` sets `expiresAt` to now, so the entry is removed on the next sweep. If zero is meant as "no expiry", handle it explicitly.

issues.title: Effect re-runs on every render and stacks intervals
issues.comment: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render — and every `setPoints` causes a render. Each run starts another 5-second interval that is never cleared, so polling multiplies until the tab stalls.

issues.title: Tooltip never hides

issues.title: Tooltip renders API text as HTML (XSS)
issues.comment: `hovered.label` comes from the revenue API, where labels are merchant-editable. Injecting it with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` lets a label like `` run script in every viewer's session. Render it as text.

issues.title: HTTP errors are parsed as revenue data
issues.comment: `fetch` doesn't reject on 4xx/5xx, so an error body is parsed and `data.points` is `undefined` — which reaches `points.map` in the chart and throws. Check `response.ok` first.

issues.title: Charge update and ledger write aren't atomic
issues.comment: The charge row is updated before `record_refund` runs, outside a transaction. If the ledger insert fails the charge shows a refund the ledger never recorded, and two concurrent refunds can both pass the remaining-amount check.

        )

issues.title: Ledger failures are logged and swallowed
issues.comment: If the insert fails, the endpoint still returns success and the ledger silently disagrees with `charges`. Re-raise after logging so the caller's transaction can roll back.

issues.title: One query per charge (N+1)
issues.comment: `refund_totals` makes a round trip for every id, so a payout report over 500 charges runs 500 queries. `WHERE charge_id = ANY($1) GROUP BY charge_id` returns the same totals in one.

data.message: Reviewing 3 files with claude-opus-5

issues.title: SQL query built from request input
issues.comment: `body.charge_id` is interpolated straight into the SQL string, so a crafted id such as `x' OR '1'='1` changes the query. The UPDATE below already uses `$1` placeholders — this lookup should too.
issues.suggested_fix: "SELECT id, merchant_id, amount, refunded FROM charges WHERE id = $1", body.charge_id

issues.title: Refunds aren't scoped to the calling merchant
issues.comment: The charge is looked up by id alone and `merchant` is never compared with `charge["merchant_id"]`, so any authenticated merchant can refund another merchant's charges by guessing an id.
issues.suggested_fix: if charge is None or charge["merchant_id"] != merchant.id:

issues.title: Money modelled as a float
issues.comment: Floats can't represent most decimal amounts exactly (`0.1 + 0.2` is `0.30000000000000004`), so repeated partial refunds drift away from the ledger. `Decimal` is already imported but unused.

issues.title: Charge update and ledger write aren't atomic
issues.comment: The charge row is updated before `record_refund` runs, outside a transaction. If the ledger insert fails the charge shows a refund the ledger never recorded, and two concurrent refunds can both pass the remaining-amount check.
issues.suggested_fix:
async with conn.transaction():
        await conn.execute(
            "UPDATE charges SET refunded = refunded + $1 WHERE id = $2 AND amount - refunded >= $1",
            body.amount,
            body.charge_id,
        )

issues.title: No tests for a money-moving endpoint
issues.comment: This adds an endpoint with several failure paths — unknown charge, over-refund, cross-merchant access — but no test file changes. Cover at least the over-refund guard and the ownership check.

data.summary: New refund endpoint. The charge lookup is injectable and isn't scoped to the calling merchant, and the refund isn't atomic.

issues.title: Ledger failures are logged and swallowed
issues.comment: If the insert fails, the endpoint still returns success and the ledger silently disagrees with `charges`. Re-raise after logging so the caller's transaction can roll back.

issues.title: One query per charge (N+1)
issues.comment: `refund_totals` makes a round trip for every id, so a payout report over 500 charges runs 500 queries. `WHERE charge_id = ANY($1) GROUP BY charge_id` returns the same totals in one.
